gbm_population_evidence.quote: Patient admitted to neurosurgery department for surgical resection of a suspected grade 3 or 4 glioma with 5-ALA (cases)

gbm_population_flag.reason: Glioblastoma is not named; only 'suspected grade 3 or 4 glioma' without IDH requirement, which counts as historical glioblastoma under D27C but could be read as high-grade glioma unspecified.

candidate_evidence.quote: A medical device (HIVEN®) detects 5-ALA-induced fluorescence from the surgical suction and gives sound feedback to the operating surgeon indicating tumor tissue
The 5-ALA (Gleolan, NX Development Corp) has been already FDA-approved since 2017 for fluorescence-guided resection of suspected WHO grade 3 or 4 gliomas.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Patient admitted to neurosurgery department for surgical resection of a suspected grade 3 or 4 glioma with 5-ALA (cases)

role_evidence.quote: In 5-ALA FGS the drug-induced fluorescence helps to visually detect tumor cells, which improves resection rates and delays tumor progression.

agents.drug_class_hint: fluorescence imaging agent for fluorescence-guided resection

coder_notes: Device study (HIVEN suction fluorescence detector), phase NA. 5-ALA is not a registered intervention but is given to all cases for fluorescence-guided surgery; listed as diagnostic_agent. Control patients (primary or secondary brain tumours without 5-ALA) are described in eligibility but there is one registered group only.
